member.name: T:Api.Controllers.DataGatewayController
member.summary: The Data Gateway's REST API: one set of routes for every entity, whatever its schema (spec 2026-11-04 §2): standard methods on the collection /api/gateway/{entity} and the record /api/gateway/{entity}/{id}, and custom methods, POST /api/gateway/{entity}:{verb}, for the operations that need a body and are not a create or an update of one record. {entity} must pass the , so a segment with a ':' never reaches a standard method and a name no schema can have is a routing 404. The controller only maps HTTP to and writes what it answers; the service authenticates the caller, checks the entity's access level and runs the operation. There is no endpoint policy here on purpose: an entity can be public, so the service decides per entity whether the caller must sign in. A failure answers in the gateway's problem shape (), and a request body is capped at ().
member.remarks: The entity is in each action's template rather than the controller's: the custom-method segment {entity}:{verb} shares its segment with the entity, and an action template can only add segments after the controller's. The final templates are the same either way, and keep the global api prefix.

member.name: T:Api.Controllers.DirectoryController
member.summary: Directory operations: create, read, list children, rename, move and delete.
member.remarks:
Creating a root directory is a separate permission from creating a nested one. Anyone with Edit on a parent may add a subdirectory, but starting a new tree at the root is a tenant-level act, so it is gated by blocks-data::directory::create-root-directory and assigned to the owner role only.
Reads that the caller may not see report 404 rather than 403 throughout. Saying "forbidden" would confirm that a directory exists, which is enough to map a tree the caller cannot open.

member.name: T:Blocks.Data.Api.Security.StyleNonce
member.summary:
The CSP style nonce for a browser.
A fresh nonce on every response changes the HTML body on every request, and a scanner comparing two responses for the same page (ZAP rule 10104, User Agent Fuzzer) then reports every page. So the nonce is derived from a random per-browser seed held in an HttpOnly cookie, keyed with a secret that never leaves the process. The same browser gets the same shell; another browser, or the same one after the cookie expires, gets a different nonce. A page cannot read the seed, and the nonce itself is hidden from CSS and the DOM.

member.summary: Host-only, Secure, HttpOnly cookie carrying the per-browser seed.

member.summary: The seed is rotated by expiry, which also rotates the nonce.
